results.title: Manipur: COCOMI Seeks Rehabilitation for 2,000 Displaced Naga People, Calls for SoO Abrogation
results.description: IMPHAL: The Coordinating Committee on Manipur Integrity (COCOMI) has urged the Central and State Government to take immediate steps to rehabilitate internally displaced persons (IDPs) from the Naga community, alleging that around 2,000 people, including women and children, have been displaced by a series of attacks allegedly carried out by Kuki militants in Ukhrul and Kamjong districts. Speaking to Organiser Weekly at the COCOMI office in Imphal on Sunday, COCOMI spokesperson Mayengbam Dhananjoy Singh condemned the reecnt attacks on Naga communities and expressed concern over the plight of those forced to flee their homes. He said the displaced people are currently taking shelter in Imphal and surrounding areas, largely in the houses of relatives and acquaintances, as the government has not established separate relief camps for them. Read More: Noney gunfight leaves three dead in Manipur; Civilian convoy comes under attack in Litan According to the Spokesperson of COCOMI, since these displaced people have not been formally recognised as internally displaced persons, they have been deprived of the humanitarian assistance and other benefits extended to IDPs residing in designated relief camps across the hill and valley districts. Raising concerns over their livelihood and immediate survival, he questioned how displaced families could sustain themselves in unfamiliar locations without employment or any regular source of income, particularly when they are dependent on relatives and friends for shelter. He maintained that the Naga community members displaced by the recent attacks are equally victims of the ongoing conflict in Manipur and deserve the same humanitarian assistance and rehabilitation measures extended to other displaced families. Reiterating COCOMI’s long-standing demands, he called for the rehabilitation and resettlement of all internally displaced persons and the abrogation of the Suspension of Operations (SoO) agreement with Kuki militant groups. He alleged that the government was effectively allowing Kuki militant groups operating under the SoO framework to enjoy immunity despite their alleged involvement in series of violence. He asserted that if the government was genuinely committed to restoring peace in Manipur, “it must demonstrate the political will to abrogate the SoO agreement and undertake a sincere and inclusive rehabilitation process for all displaced communities.”

results.title: Manipur government releases Rs. 5.88 crore as festival relief for 58,863 IDPs
results.description: The Government of Manipur released Rs. 5,88,63,000 to assist 58,863 Internally Displaced Persons for festive celebrations. This financial assistance amounts to Rs. 1,000 per eligible individual and was transferred through Direct Benefit Transfer. The funds were allocated to Deputy Commissioners in ten districts for timely distribution after verification. Yumnam Khemchand Singh expressed gratitude for the government's efforts and extended Diwali greetings to citizens.

results.title: History and International Relations
results.description: The Joint Honours Programme in History and International Relations provides students with an intellectual training in disciplines that are complementary and mutually enriching. The programme enables students to appreciate how historical events shape modern politics and how such themes are to be understood and explained through insights into political analysis (e.g. political theory, political institutions, international relations). It offers students the opportunity to analyse country-based developments across the globe and pays specific attention to the histories and politics of Africa, Europe and the Americas.

results.title: Anthropology and International Relations
results.description: The Joint Honours Programme in Anthropology and International Relations provides students with an in-depth, interdisciplinary understanding of contemporary cultures and politics, international affairs, societies, and conflict situations in their political, historical, social, cultural, economic and legal dimensions. International Relations at Queen’s is about more than just conflict, security and terrorism. It also examines such trends as globalisation and considers the challenge from the rise of Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, the process of European integration, humanitarian issues (such as poverty, development and refugees), and the role of the media in conflict. Anthropology is the study of human diversity around the world. In studying anthropology, you will learn how different societies live together and think about such topics as family, sex, religion, art, and economics and gain skills increasingly in demand in a globalized and automated world. Studying anthropology at Queen’s will allow you to examine some of the deepest and most pressing questions about human beings. Issues addressed in our modules include: Does globalisation mean the end of cultural difference? Can a post-conflict society heal? How do ritual traditions, musical performances, and art shape cultural identities? How do some people become willing to die for a group? Through classroom modules, optional placements, and your own anthropological fieldwork, you will also gain valuable skills in critical thinking, cross-cultural understanding, researching, interviewing, writing, and presenting.
